turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on going to for plans?
turns.tutor:
Here is the rule: for a plan, say am, is or are, then going to, then the plain verb.
Right: "The farmer is going to sell his sheep."
Wrong: "The farmer going to sell his sheep." The word is is missing before going to.
My example: "The pilot is going to fly to Rome." The pilot takes is, then going to, then the plain verb fly.
Now your turn. Correct:
"I going to study tonight."
